title: Series circuits practice sheet
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 96 (Series circuits practice sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 96: Electrical units, Q = It and two resistors in series. To understand electrical units and how to calculate charge, current and voltage for two resistors in series

model.title: A current of 0.50 A flows through a lamp for 2.0 minutes. Calculate the charge that passes.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: I = 0.50 A and t = 2.0 minutes = 120 s

model.title: A 6.0 V cell supplies a 4.0 ohm and an 8.0 ohm resistor in series. Calculate the current and the voltage across each resistor.

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: 0.50 A; 2.0 V and 4.0 V (which add to 6.0 V)

questions.q: A 4 Ω and 8 Ω resistor in series with 6 V. Find current. [2 marks]
questions.model: Total resistance first: 4 + 8 = 12 Ω. Then I = V ÷ R = 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5 A.

questions.q: Core: Five series circuit problems (portal worksheet): total R, current, each voltage.
questions.a: Answers in the key, e.g. 10 Ω + 20 Ω on 9 V: 30 Ω, 0.3 A, 3 V and 6 V.
questions.model: Teacher does problem 1: 10 + 20 = 30 Ω; I = 9 ÷ 30 = 0.3 A; V₁ = 3 V; V₂ = 6 V; check 3 + 6 = 9 V.

questions.q: Extend: A charge of 90 C flows through a series circuit in 3 minutes. Current?
Stretch: In series, a 6 Ω resistor has 3 V across it on a 12 V supply. Find the other resistor.
questions.a: I = 0.5 A; other voltage 9 V; R = 9 ÷ 0.5 = 18 Ω

questions.q: Two resistors of 5 Ω and 10 Ω in series. Total?
Big question: why does a second resistor in series make the current smaller?
questions.a: Total resistance increases, so for the same voltage the current is lower (I = V ÷ R).
